privacy.notes: Metadata-only MATLAB interop binding contract. It describes request and response structs, transport modes (file-import, cli-invocation, mat-exchange, c-abi-mex), diagnostics, provenance, errors, fixture gates, and module readiness without committing calculator logic or licensed payloads.

public_calculator_contract.notes: The MATLAB interop request and response structs mirror the public calculator contract fields and only add transport metadata for file import, CLI invocation, MAT exchange, and C ABI MEX handoff.

transport_modes.notes: Primary zero-build path for MATLAB consumers using readtable/parquetread on CSV and Parquet outputs from the shared core.
Primary cross-platform path for MATLAB users invoking the shared-core CLI via system() or ! with JSON/CSV output.
Fallback path for existing MATLAB workflows using save/load on .mat files converted from shared-core CSV or Parquet.
Future fallback path for in-process execution through loadlibrary/calllib requiring MATLAB compiler toolchain matching.

fields.name: mat_output_path

request_structs.notes: Single versioned MATLAB interop request envelope that mirrors the public calculator contract and adds only transport metadata.

response_structs.name: MatlabInteropResponse

fields.name: schema_version
fields.notes: Binding schema version for the response envelope.

fields.name: calculator_id
fields.notes: Echoes the public calculator identifier.

fields.name: pricing_year
fields.notes: Echoes the pricing year used during execution.

fields.name: mode
fields.notes: Declares the transport path that produced the result.

fields.name: success
fields.notes: True only when the request completed without a blocking error.

fields.name: status
fields.notes: Machine-readable execution state for the caller.

fields.name: message
fields.notes: Short human-readable summary of the result.

fields.name: warnings
fields.notes: Non-blocking warnings attached to the response.

fields.name: errors
fields.notes: Machine-readable error records emitted when the response does not succeed.

fields.name: diagnostics
fields.notes: Structured diagnostic record with pass, fail, and blocked checks.

fields.name: provenance
fields.notes: Provenance record for the request and any generated artifact.

fields.name: csv_output_path
fields.notes: CSV output path used by the file-import primary mode.

fields.name: mat_output_path
fields.notes: .mat output path used by the MAT-exchange fallback mode.

fields.name: cli_stdout
fields.notes: Captured CLI stdout output from a MATLAB system() invocation.

fields.name: fixture_gate_state
fields.notes: Observed fixture-gate outcome for the request.

fields.name: module_readiness_state
fields.notes: Observed MATLAB interop module readiness state for the binding bundle.

response_structs.notes: Single versioned MATLAB interop response envelope that captures success, diagnostics, provenance, and transport-specific outputs.

diagnostics.notes: The MATLAB interop request and response structs mirror the public calculator contract fields.
File-import and CLI-invocation are the primary transport boundaries for MATLAB consumers.
MAT-exchange and C ABI MEX are explicitly declared as fallback paths.
Fixture gates remain synthetic-only or local-only and do not expose restricted payloads.
Module readiness is tracked as declarative metadata rather than implied implementation status.

provenance.notes: Name of the contract or validation command that produced the artifact.
Stable identifier for the MATLAB interop binding contract bundle.
Path to the source manifest or fixture record used to derive the example.
Public source URL or local reference used for provenance.
Retrieval date in ISO-8601 date form.
Checksum algorithm used by the bundle.

errors.condition: request or response fields do not match the published MATLAB interop binding schema
errors.notes: Use this when the envelope is structurally invalid.

errors.condition: the shared-core CLI cannot be found or executed from MATLAB
errors.notes: The caller may retry with a different CLI path or fall back to file-import.

errors.condition: CSV or Parquet file cannot be read by MATLAB readtable or parquetread
errors.notes: The failure is transport-level, not calculator logic.

errors.condition: .mat file cannot be loaded or saved by MATLAB load/save
errors.notes: Use for MAT-exchange boundary errors in native MATLAB workflows.

errors.condition: C ABI MEX library cannot be loaded by loadlibrary or calllib
errors.notes: The failure is toolchain-level; requires Rust cdylib build and mex configuration.

errors.condition: synthetic-only or local-only fixture gate is not satisfied
errors.notes: The request must stop before any restricted payload is handled.

errors.condition: the MATLAB file/CLI adapter is unavailable or toolbox promotion is deferred
errors.notes: Use this when local adapter transport is not available, or when a caller asks for MATLAB toolbox publication evidence that is not claimed.

fixture_gates.notes: Committed examples must stay synthetic and metadata only.
Any licensed payloads stay local-only and user-supplied outside the repository.
The binding must remain pinned to the public calculator contract field set.

module_readiness.notes: The workstream has a thin file/CLI MATLAB adapter but does not assert a published MATLAB toolbox.
The file-import boundary has MATLAB helpers for existence checks, CSV/Parquet import, column validation, diagnostics, and provenance.
The CLI-invocation boundary has a MATLAB system() wrapper that builds a quoted command, captures stdout and exit status, and verifies an expected output file.

rules: Keep all examples synthetic and metadata only.
Mirror the public calculator contract fields explicitly.
Do not duplicate calculator math, thresholds, or adjustment logic in the MATLAB interop binding.
Prefer file-import or CLI-invocation first and use MAT-exchange or C ABI MEX when native MATLAB workflows or in-process execution are needed.
Keep diagnostics, provenance, and errors explicit and machine readable.
Keep fixture gates local-only and user-supplied for any licensed assets.
Treat module readiness as declarative metadata until an actual MATLAB toolbox is introduced.
